documents.title: Neurology visit - facial pain
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP
Date of visit: 02/05/2024

37-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting MS, followed in our clinic. For six months she has had bouts of severe, stabbing pain in the cheeks and jaw. Chewing sets it off, and sometimes just a light touch to the face; each jab lasts a few seconds up to a couple of minutes. She also mentions fatigue and the odd spell of blurred vision, which she had been putting down to a heavy workload.

Medications: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily; albuterol HFA prn; sertraline 50 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history: maternal aunt with MS.

Exam: Light touch over the maxillary and mandibular areas provokes the pain. Mild weakness of the left leg. Hyperreflexia.

MRI brain with and without contrast 01/29/2024: multiple periventricular white matter lesions.

Impression: Trigeminal neuralgia, in the setting of MS.
Plan: Carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily. Please check sodium, CBC and liver tests in about four weeks. Follow up in six months, sooner if the pain is not controlled.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Carbamazepine labs
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt re: neurology letter asking us to do carbamazepine safety labs. She started it 2/6. A little dizzy the first couple of days, better now, and the face pain is already less sharp. Labs ordered per PCP, she will come Mon 3/4 before work.

documents.title: Carbamazepine labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stephanie, your sodium, blood counts and liver tests are all normal on the carbamazepine. I'm sending a copy to neurology. Keep taking it as prescribed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month visit. Trigeminal neuralgia diagnosed by neurology in February, on carbamazepine 200 mg bid. No face pain since about mid-March, eating normally again. Some daytime sleepiness at first, faded. Safety labs in March were normal.
Mood steady, PHQ-9 5. Thyroid and asthma unchanged.
Exam: comfortable. Light touch to the cheeks does not trigger pain today. Lungs clear. Heart regular.
A/P: Trigeminal neuralgia controlled on carbamazepine - neuro follows. RRMS per neuro. MDD stable on sertraline 50. Hashimoto - continue 100 mcg. Physical in the fall, Pap due then.

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can I move my fall physical to early October? Work travel the last week of September.

documents.title: Re: Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Done - you're now Monday 10/7 at 8:00. Please plan for your Pap at that visit.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 08/12/2024

Trigeminal neuralgia: no attacks since March on carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily. She would like to try coming off it. Reasonable after this long without pain.

MS: no new symptoms since the last visit. Exam unchanged from February.

Plan: Taper carbamazepine - 200 mg once daily for one week, then 100 mg daily for one week, then stop. Restart and call us if the pain returns. Return in six months.

Medications after taper: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily, albuterol HFA prn. NKDA.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Outside letter review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Neurology letter reviewed. Carbamazepine being tapered off over 2 weeks; removed from active med list. Trigeminal neuralgia remains on problem list.

reports.text: Specimen adequate, endocervical/transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
38 yo, yearly visit.
Interval: off carbamazepine since late August, no face pain since. MS quiet, saw neuro in August.
Mood: a bit flatter since the summer, still functioning; PHQ-9 6. No SI. Wants to stay on 50 for now and see.
Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg, sertraline 50 mg, albuterol prn. NKDA.
Gyn: periods regular; Pap/HPV due (last 2019).
Exam: thyroid normal, lungs clear, heart regular, breasts without masses, abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions; Pap/HPV collected. Neuro: hyperreflexia, gait steady.
A/P: Pap/HPV done. Flu and COVID today. CMP, CBC, TSH. Mammogram screening starts at 40 - will order at next physical. Mood - watch; revisit in January. Continue meds.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: your Pap and HPV test are normal, so the next one is in five years. Thyroid, blood counts and chemistry panel all normal too.

documents.title: 90-day refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill requests: levothyroxine 100 mcg #90 and sertraline 50 mg #90. Both on active list, seen in October. Approved, 3 refills.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in as planned. Mood has slid over the past couple of months: low most days, pulling back from friends, forcing herself through work. Sleep okay. No SI, no plan, asked directly. PHQ-9 13, up from 6 in October. Taking sertraline 50 every day.
Exam: flat affect, otherwise well. Lungs clear.
A/P: MDD, single episode, moderate - symptoms back up on 50 mg after a good stretch. Increase sertraline to 100 mg daily. Reviewed what to watch for with a dose change. Portal check-in in 2-3 weeks, visit in about 6-8 weeks, sooner if worse. Psychiatry is an option again if this doesn't help - she'd like to try the dose first.

documents.title: Shaky hands
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Mood maybe a little better on the higher dose. But for the last couple of weeks my hands have been shaky, worst when I'm writing or holding a coffee. Not my usual MS stuff, it's both hands. Should I be worried?

documents.title: Re: Shaky hands
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know. Dr. would like to see you in person - we have Monday 2/3 at 9:30. Keep taking your medicines as usual until then, and call if you get new weakness or trouble walking.

conditions.label: Drug-induced tremor due to sertraline (enhanced physiologic tremor)

documents.title: Office Visit - tremor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About three weeks of shaking in both hands, worse when she writes or holds a mug, not there when her hands are resting in her lap. Started roughly a week after sertraline went from 50 to 100 mg on 1/8. No head injury. No new meds or supplements otherwise, caffeine unchanged, no palpitations or heat intolerance. Mood a little better.

O: Vitals normal. Fine, fast tremor of both outstretched hands, which gets more pronounced on finger-to-nose. No rest tremor, no rigidity, no bradykinesia. Gait steady. Neuro otherwise at her baseline.

A/P
1. Tremor - enhanced physiologic tremor, timing fits the sertraline increase. Thyroid overactivity on replacement would be the other thing to exclude: TSH, CBC, lytes and glucose today. Plan to drop sertraline back to 50 mg daily.
2. MDD - partial improvement at 100; we'll see how she does back at 50 and reconsider (psychiatry, another agent) if mood slips.
Follow up 6 weeks.

Addendum 2/4: CBC, TSH, electrolytes and glucose all normal. Sertraline 50 mg sent; she has 50s at home already. Drug-induced tremor due to sertraline added to problem list.

conditions.label: Drug-induced tremor due to sertraline (enhanced physiologic tremor)

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back on sertraline 50 for six weeks. The shaking faded within about ten days and has not come back. Mood has held - not where it was a year ago but better than January, PHQ-9 8. No SI.
Exam: no tremor with arms outstretched or finger-nose today.
A/P: Drug-induced tremor - resolved after dose reduction. MDD on sertraline 50, improving; keep as is, low threshold for psychiatry. Recheck in 3 months (video fine).

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: acute right upper quadrant pain with tenderness and elevated transaminases.
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast, portal venous phase, with multiplanar reformats.
Findings: Small subcapsular hematoma along the right hepatic lobe. No active contrast extravasation. No free fluid in the abdomen or pelvis. Liver otherwise enhances normally. Gallbladder, bile ducts, pancreas, spleen, adrenals and kidneys normal. Bowel normal in caliber. Appendix normal. Uterus and ovaries unremarkable. Postoperative change of prior pelvic fixation, healed. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: Small subcapsular hematoma of the right hepatic lobe without active extravasation or free fluid.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT AND OBSERVATION UNIT
Date of service: 02/04/2026 - 02/05/2026

CC: Abdominal pain.

HPI: 39 yo F with MS, Hashimoto thyroiditis, asthma and depression, with a history of a medication side effect, presents with severe abdominal pain that came on suddenly last night and has grown steadily worse. No nausea or vomiting, no change in bowel habits. She does not describe a fall or other injury. Appears anxious and has trouble keeping eye contact during the interview.
PMH: as above; previously hospitalized for a pelvic fracture after a fall down the stairs, treated with ORIF.
Home meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily; albuterol HFA prn; sertraline 50 mg daily. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, social alcohol, marketing manager.

Exam: Multiple bruises of varying ages on both arms. A single bruise on the abdomen that looks recent. RUQ tenderness with guarding, no rebound.

Labs: Hgb 12.5, WBC 9.0, plt 250. AST 150, ALT 125, alk phos 100. Amylase 50, lipase 45.
CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast: small subcapsular hematoma of the right hepatic lobe, no active extravasation, no free fluid.

Assessment: Hepatic injury.

Course: Kept overnight in observation for pain control and a repeat count. Morning Hgb 12.2. Pain improved; tolerating diet.
Safety: Asked privately, without anyone else present, whether she feels safe at home and whether anyone has hurt her. She said she is safe and did not want to talk further. Declined social work. Given printed resource information including a 24-hour hotline.

Discharge: Acetaminophen as needed, avoid NSAIDs and strenuous activity for now. PCP follow-up within one week; return for worsening pain, dizziness or fainting.

cc: PCP

documents.title: ED records received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED and observation records from 2/4-2/5 received by fax, CT report attached. Scanned and routed to PCP. Pt booked 2/11.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Seen at the ED 2/4 with sudden severe abdominal pain; CT showed a small subcapsular hematoma of the right lobe of the liver, AST 150 / ALT 125, held overnight with a stable count, sent home on acetaminophen. Today she says the pain is much better, a dull ache under the right ribs if she twists. Eating normally. No fever, no lightheadedness. She does not offer how it happened and I did not press beyond asking once.

O: Vitals normal. Fading bruises on both forearms. Abdomen soft, mild RUQ tenderness, no guarding.

A/P
1. Hepatic injury - clinically improving. LFTs today, repeat in a month. No contact sports or heavy lifting until we see normal values.
2. Safety - Spoke with her alone. Asked if anyone at home or elsewhere is hurting her or scaring her. She said no, that she is fine, and didn't want to go into it. Told her she can bring it up with me any time, by phone or portal, and that we can help quietly if things ever change. Gave the same hotline info the ED did.
3. MDD on sertraline 50 - PHQ deferred today.

Result addendum 2/12: AST 61, ALT 68 - coming down. Repeat 3/11.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stephanie, your liver numbers are already about halfway back toward normal (AST 61, ALT 68). That fits with healing. Let's recheck on March 11. Reach out any time - for this or anything else.

documents.title: Re: Liver tests
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. I'll come in on the 11th.

documents.title: Lab reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Reminder that your repeat liver blood test is due this Wednesday 3/11. No appointment needed, walk in any time 7-11.

documents.title: Liver tests normal
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver tests are back to normal. You can go back to your usual activity. I'll see you in May for a regular check.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, baseline study. Breasts are scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcification or architectural distortion in either breast. Skin and axillae unremarkable.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. No abdominal pain since early March; LFTs normalized 3/11. Back to her walks. Mood okay, PHQ-9 6, no SI. Asked again, alone, whether things are okay at home: she says yes. Mammogram in April normal.
Exam: abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No bruising seen today. Lungs clear.
A/P: Hepatic injury - resolved. MDD on sertraline 50 - stable. RRMS per neurology. Hashimoto - continue. Physical in August.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill requests for levothyroxine 100 mcg and sertraline 50 mg, 90-day each, plus albuterol HFA. All on the current list; approved per PCP. Physical on the books for 8/20.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
40 yo, yearly visit (first one in her forties, as she pointed out).
Interval: liver injury from February resolved, LFTs normal in March. No abdominal symptoms. MS: no new attacks she reports; neurology following. Face pain has stayed away. No tremor.
Mood: steady, PHQ-9 5. No SI.
Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily, albuterol HFA prn. NKDA.
HM: mammogram 4/2026 normal; Pap/HPV 10/2024 normal; Tdap 2020. Colon screening starts at 45. Flu and COVID once available this fall, nurse visit.
Exam: well. Thyroid normal size, no nodules. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Breasts without masses. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without bruising. Neuro: hyperreflexia, steady gait.
A/P: CMP, CBC, TSH today. Continue current meds. Follow-up in November.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of your labs from yesterday are normal, including thyroid and liver tests. No changes. See you in November.

documents.title: Re: Physical labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thank you! Can I get the flu shot at the November visit or should I come in sooner?

documents.title: Re: Physical labs
documents.author: RN
documents.body: We expect flu vaccine in late September - I'll message you when it's in so you can come for a quick nurse visit rather than wait.
